expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: immersion as psychological state of envelopment (presence = involvement + immersion)

expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: six characterizations of presence; presence as perceptual illusion of non-mediation; perceptual vs. psychological immersion
expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.critique_anchor: Praised for synthetic move (six categories) but critiqued via McMahan's application to Myst III — fails to yield rich practical analysis; reduces to feature-list pigeonholing.

expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: perceptual / psychological / social-realism immersion (operationalizing Lombard + Ditton on Myst III)
expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.critique_anchor: Sustained critique: descriptive feature-listing; claims (social realism) apply trivially to any game in genre; fails to elucidate game-specific affordances.

expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: immersive fallacy critique (immersion as absorption, Tetris-immersibility)
expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.critique_anchor: Partial endorsement (correctly attacks mimetic-realism imperative) + sustained critique (sidelines spatiality as defining feature of VE immersion; conflates absorption with transportation).

expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: immersion (within-frame schema) vs. engagement (extra-textual critical stance)
expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.critique_anchor: Praised for attentional-continuum recognition (conscious↔unconscious involvement); critiqued for collapsing ergodic/non-ergodic distinction (Balzac/Dickens/Krantz = Space Invaders).

Critiqued for metaphor-mixing: levels 1-2 = absorption, level 3 = transportation; exacerbates the definitional confusion they set out to resolve. Cairns et al. (2006) follow-on study inherits the same mixed-metaphor flaw.

expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.model_label: multidimensional 'gameplay experience model' — sensory / challenge-based / imaginative immersion
expected_pre_calleja_immersion_models.critique_anchor: Acknowledged contribution (multidimensionality + medium-specificity); critiqued for empirically deriving 'immersion' meaning from child interviews — collapses academic-technical sense into colloquial sense.

expected_ontological_grounding_anchors.work: The Question Concerning Technology and Other Essays (New York: Harper & Row)
expected_ontological_grounding_anchors.context: Cited in the course of arguing (contra Slater's fidelity-determinist orchestra example) that interpretation/agency mediate presence: 'When we are faced with experiences we cannot readily interpret, our mode of being becomes more critically removed and we must actively think about what we are doing (Heidegger, 1993).' No engagement with Sein und Zeit, Dasein, In-der-Welt-sein, Zuhandenheit, or any SZ-era ontological-phenomenological apparatus. This is the late-Heidegger of technology critique, not the SZ-Heidegger that would ground the dissertation's BCAP-anchored Layer A augmentation.
expected_ontological_grounding_anchors.implication: This is the SOLE ontological-grounding-related cite in the entire book. All other ontological-grounding edges (to BCAP, Phantasia Cluster, Bowin AMT) remain anticipatory-projection (dissertation).
